summary: DOSBox-X 2026.05.02 Vga save blob layout for Wiz6 mode-0x0D (320x200 EGA 16-color). VRAM (vga.mem.linear) starts at blob offset 0x84000, stored as 4-plane dword-interleaved (plane P at blob[0x84000 + vgaAddr*4 + P]). Palette pipeline: raw 4-bit EGA attribute → wiz6-main AC table (wroot.exe 0x2043) → BIOS-default DAC index → 6-bit RGB → 8-bit RGB. The blob's AC register field at 0x82FC2 holds BIOS default values (NOT the wiz6-main game table) and must NOT be used for decoding. The game draws the CHARACTER MENU using only EGA planes 0 and 3: plane 3 for background (attr 8 = dark-gray), plane 0 overlaid for borders (attr 9 = light-gray via AC) and text (attr 1 = white via AC). Planes 1 and 2 are never written for this UI mode; the save correctly reflects that.

findings.claim: VGA VRAM (vga.mem.linear) starts at blob offset 0x84000 in every captured save state. The range 0x80000–0x83FFF is the VGA register/state dump, NOT VRAM.

blob_layout.0x000000-0x07FFFF: mostly-zero VGA state header (512 KB, < 0.1% non-zero)
blob_layout.0x080000-0x083FFF: VGA register state dump: CRTC at 0x82F8C, AC regs at 0x82FC2 (BIOS default, NOT wiz6-main), DAC at 0x82FE9 (768 bytes), EGA lookup tables through 0x83FFF

findings.claim: VGA VRAM is stored as 4-plane dword-interleaved: for VGA address A and plane P, the byte is at blob[0x84000 + A*4 + P].

evidence.observable: Decoding with interleaved formula at base 0x84000 produces correct structured game screens (black windows, dark-gray background, light-gray frames, white text). Planar layout (separate 64KB planes) produces wrong colors.
evidence.stride: 40 bytes/plane/row × 8 bits/byte = 320 pixels/row, confirmed by CRTC offset reg 0x13 = 0x14 = 20 → row stride 40

findings.claim: CRTC display-start address = 0 (registers 0x0C/0x0D both = 0x00) in all captured saves. No page flipping at any captured game state.
CRTC offset register (reg 0x13) = 0x14 = 20 → row stride = 40 bytes per row per plane. Correct for 320-pixel-wide mode 0x0D.

DAC palette is at blob offset 0x82FE9, 768 bytes (256 entries × 3 channels × 6-bit values). Entries 0–31 match BIOS-default EGA (low-intensity 0–15, high-intensity 16–23, low-intensity repeat 24–31). Entries 56–255 are zero (black).

evidence.method: direct read from blob across all saves
evidence.note: DAC is invariant across all saves. Used as the second stage of the AC→DAC pipeline.

findings.claim: Pixel→RGB uses the wiz6-main AC table (wroot.exe 0x2043) composed with the BIOS-default DAC. Pipeline: raw_index → WIZ6_MAIN_AC[raw_index] → DAC[dac_entry] → 8-bit RGB. The blob's AC register field at 0x82FC2 holds BIOS-default EGA attribute controller values and must NOT be used.

evidence.why_bios_ac_is_wrong: The blob's AC field at 0x82FC2 holds the BIOS-default EGA attribute controller values, which differ from the wiz6-main table the game programs. Decoding with the blob AC gives white windows on light-gray background (inverted luminance). The game programs INT 10h AH=10h AL=02h with wiz6-main at startup (see docs/re/palette-discovery.md). Always use WIZ6_MAIN_AC.

findings.claim: The character menu is drawn using only EGA planes 0 and 3. Plane 3 carries the background fill (attr 8 = dark-gray). Plane 0 is overlaid for frame borders (attr 9 = light-gray via wiz6-main AC) and window interior text (attr 1 = white). Planes 1 and 2 are never written for this UI mode.

evidence.method: plane-by-plane non-zero byte count across saves 1–3
evidence.plane1_nonzero_vga_addrs: 10–13 (all in DOSBox-X internal-state noise area, rows 15–16 only)
evidence.plane2_nonzero_vga_addrs: 13–85 (mostly DOSBox-X noise; save 3 has more from cursor/highlight state)
evidence.plane3_nonzero_vga_addrs: ~4500–4560 (background fill for the entire dark-gray screen region)
evidence.implication: The combined plane0+plane3 set gives EGA attribute 9 for border pixels (both planes set at border positions because background fill was not cleared before border draw). Window interior area has plane3=0 (explicitly cleared), leaving attr 0 = black. Text rows have plane3=0 (window clear) + plane0=set_for_glyph_bits = attr 1 = white.

findings.claim: DOSBox-X writes ~170 internal-state bytes into vga.mem.linear at VGA addresses 621–646 (screen rows 15–16, right-side columns 21–46) and scattered positions (rows 18–23, 49–54, 121–131). These produce ~161 noise pixels (< 0.3% of screen). They are invariant across all captured saves.

evidence.example: VGA addr 630 (row 15 col_byte 30): bytes (03,04,05,06) = sequential counter values, not pixel data
evidence.decision: Not masked — visual impact is negligible and the base is confirmed correct.

validation_save1.content_visible: Dark-gray background, black window interior, light-gray double-line frames, white text at bottom: PORTRAIT / EXIT / CREATE PC / REVIEW PC / DELETE PC / RENAME PC

validation_save2.content_visible: Same layout, text at bottom: CREATE PC / EXIT (minimal text = 0.5% white, passes >0.3% threshold)

validation_save3.save: tools/dosbox/save/3.sav (CHARACTER MENU — full roster, no CREATE PC)
validation_save3.content_visible: Same layout, text: EXIT / REVIEW PC / DELETE PC / RENAME PC / PORTRAIT. Yellow highlight on selected option from wiz6-main AC color 13 (olive/yellow).
